notes.text: Kirill Marchenko is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Nick Blankenburg is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 52% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 71:15 together, about what it had with Blankenburg (48%).
Jack Roslovic is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 24 games, up from 6% last season.
Ryan Pulock is out (shoulder injury) and missed their last game. Matthew Schaefer has taken his spot beside Adam Pelech.
Logan Stanley returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, down from 37% last season.

story.head: Barzal’s favorite opponent
paras: The Maple Leafs are winless in nine (0-8-1), while the Islanders (11-6-5) beat Detroit 3-2 on Saturday. The teams have split two meetings this season. Going in, the Maple Leafs are last in the Atlantic (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Islanders third in the Metropolitan (tied for 15th).

The Maple Leafs have played better than their record (.380) says: their chances are worth about .482, mostly because they’re 3-10 in one-goal games. The Islanders’ record (.614) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.504), largely thanks to their goaltending. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.
In their nine-game skid, the Maple Leafs have been outscored 36-18, including 24-15 at 5-on-5.

The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st) and lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), but have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Islanders, by contrast, have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st). They also get their defensemen shooting (2nd). They also roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), so the Islanders roll four lines, but the Leafs lean on their top six. The Maple Leafs’ power play (10th) could do real damage against the Islanders’ penalty kill (29th), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way.

Auston Matthews (14 G / 19 A / 33 P in 25 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, with five goals in six games against the Islanders since 2023-24. William Nylander (11 G / 14 A / 25 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Simon Holmström (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 22 GP) has a team-high ten goals, with eight points in his last five games.
Anthony Stolarz (5-5-1 / .902 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to go for Toronto. Ilya Sorokin (9-4-2 / .918 SV% in 15 GS) has been outstanding for the Islanders and is expected to start.
